rounds.fact: Bebo was massively popular in the UK and Ireland during the mid-2000s, at one point ranking as the third-most-visited social network in the US before AOL bought it for $850 million in 2008.
Kickstarter launched in 2009 and popularized the all-or-nothing crowdfunding model, where projects only get funded if they hit their goal, a rule meant to protect backers.
HotBot launched in 1996 with a distinctly loud, colorful interface, and was one of the first search engines to index the full text of pages rather than just titles and keywords.
Tripod was a major free website-builder alongside GeoCities and Angelfire, and was eventually bought by Lycos as part of its portal strategy in the late 90s.
Yahoo Finance became one of the most-used sources for free stock quotes on the early web, at a time when real-time market data elsewhere often required a paid subscription.
